subject: Competitive benchmark grant — usage split, reporting, and approval
messages:
From: Sara Levin <sara.levin@optimed.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood trial credits for RFP bake-off

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. OptiMed is running a head-to-head bake-off across three vendors (Redwood, CompetitorX, and CloudGen) focused on inpatient triage and discharge-summary generation. Procurement asked me to get a clearer picture of what trial/benchmark credits Redwood can extend and any restrictions on usage (e.g., token caps, regional limits, model/quantization constraints).

A few specifics that would help our procurement and ML teams:
- Can credits be split by region (US vs EU) for compliance reasons?
- Are credits usable for streaming and embeddings or only generation?
- Do you require an evaluation report or do you provide a usage template?
- Typical expiration window on eval credits?

We want to finalize the bake-off budget this week. Happy to jump on a quick call if easier.

Cheers,
Sara Levin
Head of ML Platforms
OptiMed Solutions

---
Attachment: bakeoff_scope.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sara Levin <sara.levin@optimed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood trial credits for RFP bake-off

Sara —

Appreciate the details and the timeline. Short answers up front, then I've cc'd Ben (program ops) and Karthik (sales lead) to scope the right package.

- Yes, we can partition credits across regions; we just need to flag data residency constraints in the agreement.
- Credits are generally valid for generation (streaming and non-streaming) and embeddings, but there are usage guardrails around high-volume KV-cache and pre-warm allocations.
- We provide a usage report template and can accept a short evaluation summary from you for compliance.
- Standard expiry is 90 days from issuance; we can discuss a 120-day window for enterprise RFPs.

Ben / Karthik — can you propose a recommended allocation for OptiMed (estimate of tokens/embeddings + any pro-bono engineering time), and note any billing/contract language we should include? Sara, if you can share expected monthly token volumes for the trial and which regions will host the tests that will speed this up.

Best,
Naomi
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

---

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood trial credits for RFP bake-off

Naomi / team —

Thanks, Naomi. Proposed allocation (initial recommendation):
- US: 500k generation tokens (supports streaming and non-streaming).
- EU: 150k generation tokens.
- Embeddings pool: 50k embedding units (for vector search experiments).
- Reserve: 100k tokens for model/pathway switching during warmup (we tag these separately).

Guardrails / policy notes:
- Credits are not usable for model training or fine-tuning jobs.
- High-throughput KV-cache pre-warm requests (>200 concurrent sessions) require advance notice and are billed separately.
- Expiration: 120 days with an optional 30-day one-time extension upon request.

I'll draft a short credit agreement (pdf) with the above and include a usage_report_template.xlsx. Marcus — is the above acceptable from a finance exposure perspective for a mid-market RFP?

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: redwood_credit_proposal_draft.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Sara Levin <sara.levin@optimed.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@optimed.com
Date: 2026-09-21T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood trial credits for RFP bake-off

Thanks Naomi / Ben — that allocation looks sensible. To help you narrow the split:
- Production-like tests will run in us-west (primary) and eu-west (sanitised subset).
- Expected gross tokens over the 90–120 day window: ~450k generation tokens and ~30k embedding units.
- We will not attempt any fine-tuning during the benchmark.

Procurement also asked for two compliance items:
1) a statement that trial data will not be used for model training;
2) an audit-ready usage report at the end of the trial (schema + per-route token counts).

If you can send the draft agreement and the usage_report_template, procurement will fast-track internal sign-off.

—Sara

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood trial credits for RFP bake-off

Looping Marcus for explicit finance approval since OptiMed is asking for the 120-day expiration and region-split. Marcus — per Ben's proposal the exposure is ~800k tokens equivalent if they exercise the reserve; we can mark it as "conditional credit" for the bake-off and require the completed usage template and one-page evaluation report as acceptance criteria. Also recommend we include a clause: credits revert to paid usage after the expiration/extension.

If Marcus signs off, I'll send the DocuSign link for the credit agreement and flag the HubSpot deal to move to "Committed—Eval".

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T09:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood trial credits for RFP bake-off

Karthik / team —

Finance approves the conditional credit allocation with these constraints:
- Total exposure capped at the equivalent of 800k tokens.
- Credits issued after DocuSign and receipt of the signed one-page MSA addendum.
- OptiMed must submit the completed usage_report_template.xlsx within 10 days of test completion; otherwise credits revert to billable usage.
- Extension policy: single 30-day extension subject to review; no further extensions without executive sign-off.

I've attached a signed draft (optimed_credit_agreement_draft.pdf) with the above language. Charge code: FIN-OPTI-26.

Marcus Lin
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: optimed_credit_agreement_draft.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sara Levin <sara.levin@optimed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, procurement@optimed.com
Date: 2026-09-22T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood trial credits for RFP bake-off — next steps

Sara —

Great, we're aligned and Finance has signed off on the conditional package. Next steps from our side:
1) Karthik will send the DocuSign link for the credit addendum (you should see it by EOD PST).
2) Ben will deliver the usage_report_template.xlsx and a short "how-to" for the per-route token counts.
3) DocuSign + procurement signature triggers issuance of the credits (120-day period).
4) OptiMed delivers the final evaluation report within 10 days of the test window; we'll review together and flag any billing conversions.

Attachments: usage_report_template.xlsx, redwood_promo_slabs_v2.pdf

If anything changes on your side (test region mix or expected token burn), please let us know ASAP so we can adjust allocations before issuing the credits. Looking forward to working with your team on the bake-off.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
